notes: company_ids hold only IDs cross-checked against SIG-derived sources; the full SIG list (--update-db) is authoritative and wins over this file
oui_confidence: alert | possible | info:<category>; used by scanner.py only. Flock OUIs other than B4:1E:52 are shared component-vendor prefixes = weak evidence
unverified_ouis are kept for review and are NOT used for matching
wearables_audio = watches/rings/bands; audio_wearables = headphones/speakers/media; scanner.py maps both to its WEARABLES-AUDIO-MEDIA group
Skimmer module names are weak evidence: the same generic BLE serial modules are used in thousands of hobby projects. Treat as 'possible', never 'alert'.
2026-10-08 cleanup: removed collision-prone generic tokens (e.g. kali, motive, tws, police) from the expansion.
Name terms match as whole words on the lowercased name (underscores/spaces collapsed): a term may not touch a letter on either side, digits are fine.
le_target_names is not read by the scanner; use categories.law_enforcement_tactical / alert_names instead.

2026-10-08 round 2: 7 new panels (smart glasses/AI wearables, FPV/RC, crypto wallets + security keys, hotels/hospitals/venues, EV/e-bike/scooter, outdoor/sat/off-grid power, home AV). Terms re-homed from older categories so first-match doesn't hide them.

2026-10-09 round 3: new hunting_trail_woods panel (trail/game cameras, hunting optics + rangefinders, e-callers, hunting-dog collars, woods radios/sat, wildlife telemetry, forestry/survey gear). Hunting-dog collars (garmin alpha/astro/tt 15/t5, sportdog, dogtra) re-homed from pet_trackers so first-match shows them here.

2026-10-09 round 4: new panels for e-readers/e-ink/smart notepads, hearing/vision/mobility assistive tech, farm/ranch/rural, utilities/SCADA/smart-city, construction/mining/oil-gas, military/defense, corrections monitoring, aviation/marine, fleet/RV, cameras/production, makers/3D/craft. Kindle/Kobo/reMarkable/Boox/Fire terms re-homed out of laptops_tablets so first-match shows them in the e-reader panel. corrections_offender_monitoring is a normal panel (not tactical tier) to avoid false police alerts.

2026-10-09 round 4b: pruned new panels to Bluetooth-advertising device families only. Removed companies, vehicles/tractors/heavy machinery/bike models, apps/protocols, generic descriptions, and Wi-Fi/cellular/proprietary-RF-only gear. corrections_offender_monitoring panel removed (devices do not advertise identifiable BLE names). Remaining terms are brand/product-line names expected to appear in BLE local names; not verified against live captures.

2026-10-09 round 5: law-enforcement Bluetooth gear. Alert tier (law_enforcement_tactical): Axon/TASER incl. Signal Sidearm/Vehicle/Performance Power Magazine, Motorola Holster Aware + SVX + V700/VB400/LEX F10, Utility smart holster/body worn, Safariland CAS 7TS holster sensor, Safe Fleet holster activation, VIEVU, Digital Ally. Possible tier: generic holster-sensor and Safariland/Safe Fleet brand names (also civilian/commercial). alert_names now carries the Flock BLE names from the old le_target_names (fs ext battery, pigvision, ^flock-, ^penguin). Names are brand/product strings, not verified against live captures.

2026-10-09 round 5: ESP32/ESP-IDF default BLE names + chip-variant spellings (esp32c3, esp32s3 ...), M5/LilyGO/Unexpected Maker/Arduino/Nordic/ST/SiLabs/TI/Infineon dev-board names, more hacker gadgets (Bangle.js/Puck.js, CatSniffer, Meshtastic hardware, jammers, sub-GHz modules), 26 confirmed Espressif OUIs as info:smart_iot (public-address ESP32 BLE only; commercial ESP-based products match too, so these are low-confidence 'Espressif-based device' hints), 31 more kept in unverified_ouis, missing gaming handhelds (AYANEO, AYN, OneXPlayer, AOKZOE, GPD Win family, Miyoo ...), and a new panel handheld_computers_umpc for non-gaming handheld computers (GPD Pocket/MicroPC/P2 Max, UMPCs, ClockworkPi/Linux handhelds, PDAs, rugged handheld terminals, survey controllers). Regex rules added for PROV_xxxxxx, nimble-ble*, ESP_GATTS/SPP/HID/BLE names and CircuitPython.

2026-10-10 cleanup: (1) moved misfiled terms to the right panel (peripherals, music gear and toys got their own panels; smart locks/cameras -> security; camera brands -> cameras; telematics -> fleet; hearing aids -> accessibility; ham radios -> outdoor comms; pocket label/photo printers -> makers). (2) removed software/apps/protocols, company-only names, generic phrases, ordinary words that false-match, and gear that does not advertise a Bluetooth name (SDRs/probes, Wi-Fi/enterprise networking, QR/USB-only wallets and keys, USB mics, SSDs). (3) removed exact duplicates and every term already identified, with the same result, by a shorter term or by scanner.py's built-in rules (checked against the real classifier: no kept term changed category except the deliberate moves). (4) dropped the unused le_target_names list. Removed terms and reasons are in scanner_config_removed_terms.json.

2026-10-10 research: added 18 community-list OUIs (Axon D8:1F:65, ShotSpotter, Digital Ally, VieVu, Utility, Zepcam, Genetec, Elsag...) to unverified_ouis only (NOT matched; mostly Wi-Fi/Ethernet prefixes, no BLE confirmation). Added alert name 'bwcdevice' (Axon body-cam advertising tag) and possible name ^fs-<hex> (Flock battery pack).

vendor_categories: {category: [vendor names]} maps a SIG company / IEEE OUI owner to a category (plain text = whole word, 're:' = regex). It is the weakest evidence: any name, service or Apple/Microsoft rule beats it. The session report's 'Adv clues' column shows the company IDs and service UUIDs behind each device so you can write the next rules.

2026-10-11 round 4: service_rules for FCF1/FEF3 (Google), Fi collar (128-bit 57B40001…), Zebra FE79, Fitbit FD62; Fi collar name regex; TV terms (crystal uhd, uhd tv, [tv]) so Samsung TVs stop landing in smartphones.

schema.categories: {category_key: [terms]} - unknown keys automatically get a dashboard panel (icon/colour from category_meta or defaults)
schema.category_meta: {key: {icon,title,color,civilian}} to style a panel, or {tier:'alert'|'possible'} to route the category to the tactical panel
schema.category_aliases: {alias: real_category} merge several config lists into one existing category
schema.tactical_categories: [keys] whose terms raise an ALERT in the tactical panel
schema.category_regex: {category_key: [regex]} raw regexes (case-insensitive) matched on the normalised name
schema.alert_names / possible_names: [term or 're:regex'] direct tactical alert / possible-tier name rules, independent of categories
schema.custom_names / ignore_list: MAC -> display name, MACs to hide
